properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 23 at 2:16PM EDT by NWS Miami FL
properties.description:
At 216 PM EDT, National Weather Service meteorologists were tracking
a strong thunderstorm capable of producing a waterspout near Ocean
Ridge, moving south at 15 mph.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts of 45 to 50 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous waters. Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs
and blow around unsecured objects.

Locations impacted include...
Boynton Beach, Delray Beach, Lake Worth, Palm Beach, Ocean Ridge,
Lantana, Hypoluxo, South Palm Beach, Gulf Stream, and Briny Breezes.
properties.instruction:
These winds can down small tree limbs and branches, and blow around
unsecured small objects. Seek shelter in a safe building until the
storm passes.

Funnel clouds can touch down and produce waterspouts. Although
typically weak and short lived, a landfalling waterspout can cause
property damage and serious injury.

NWSheadline: A strong thunderstorm will impact portions of east central Palm Beach County through 300 PM EDT

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 23 at 12:15PM MDT until October 24 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Animas River Near Cedar Hill affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Animas River near Cedar Hill.

* WHEN...Until Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 11.5 feet, The river would be near an all time high.
Areas along the river that never before experienced flooding will
likely be inundated as water levels continue to rise.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Friday the stage was 10.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Friday was 10.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 11.3 feet
late this afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage just
after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 10.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 11.3
feet on 09/06/1970.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Saturday afternoon at noon MDT.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 23 at 12:15PM MDT until October 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central New Mexico, including the following
area, South Central Mountains.

* WHEN...From 6 PM MDT this evening through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- A longer duration period of numerous showers and thunderstorms
will set up this evening, with activity redeveloping again in the
afternoon Saturday and persisting into Saturday evening. Recent
wildfire burn scars in Lincoln county remain vulnerable to abrupt
runoff and flash flooding. While individual showers and
thunderstorms will typically produce rainfall amounts of 0.25 to
0.75 inch, multiple rounds of storms will increase the risk of
flash flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

SMWMFL

The National Weather Service in Miami has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Lake Worth to Delay Beach Beach FL out 10 NM...

* Until 245 PM EDT.

* At 211 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located near Ocean Ridge, moving south at 10 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Locations impacted include...
Ocean Ridge, South Palm Beach, Manalapan, Briny Breezes, Gulf
Stream, Delray Beach, and Palm Beach.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

Report severe weather to the Coast Guard or the National Weather
Service. You can also share your report with NWS Miami on Facebook
and Twitter.

to excessive rainfall over the previous 48 hours.
